record.original_question: Let G_{p,1} be the induced subgraph of the Paley graph G_p on the vertices adjacent to 0 (the 1-localization). Is the Lovász theta number of this localized graph asymptotic to √(p/2), that is, does ϑ(G_{p,1}) ∼ √(p/2) as p → ∞ through primes congruent to 1 modulo 4?

evidence.quote: Let G_p,1 denote the induced subgraph on the vertices adjacent to the node 0, which we call the 1-localization ... It was observed empirically in [MMP19b] that ϑ(G_p,1) ∼ √(p/2) ... Conjecture 26. ϑ(G_p,1) ∼ √(p/2) (for p ≡ 1 (mod 4) prime) where G_p,1 is the 1-localization of the Paley Graph described above.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod{4}$, let $G_p$ be the Paley graph on the vertex set $\mathbb{F}_p$, in which two distinct vertices $x, y \in \mathbb{F}_p$ are adjacent if and only if $x - y$ is a nonzero quadratic residue modulo $p$ (this is well-defined since $-1$ is a square in $\mathbb{F}_p$). Let $G_{p,1}$ denote the "1-localization" of $G_p$: the induced subgraph of $G_p$ on the set $N(0) = \{x \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times : x \text{ is a nonzero quadratic residue mod } p\}$ of vertices adjacent to $0$.

Recall that the Lovász theta number $\vartheta(H)$ of a graph $H$ on vertex set $V$ is defined by
$$\vartheta(H) = \max \sum_{i,j \in V} B_{ij},$$
where the maximum is over symmetric positive semidefinite matrices $B \in \mathbb{R}^{V \times V}$ with $\mathrm{tr}(B) = 1$ and $B_{ij} = 0$ whenever $i \neq j$ and $\{i,j\}$ is an edge of $H$.

Determine whether
$$\vartheta(G_{p,1}) \sim \sqrt{p/2} \qquad \text{as } p \to \infty \text{ through primes } p \equiv 1 \pmod 4.$$
artifact.category_tag: Lovász theta number of Paley graphs
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that $\vartheta(G_{p,1}) \sim \sqrt{p/2}$ for the 1-localization of the Paley graph appears to remain open. It is stated as an empirical observation/conjecture in problem collections from the Paley-graph clique-number circle of problems. Hanson–Petridis proved $\omega(G_p) \le (1+o(1))\sqrt{p/2}$ for the full Paley graph, but no published proof of the asymptotic $\vartheta(G_{p,1}) \sim \sqrt{p/2}$ for the 1-localization is found.

status_evidence.title: On the clique number of the Paley Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture: ϑ(G_{p,1}) ∼ √(p/2) for p ≡ 1 (mod 4) prime, where G_{p,1} is the 1-localization of the Paley Graph.
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open conjecture based on empirical observation.

status_evidence.title: The Lovász number of random circulant graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The independence number of Paley graphs can be upper bounded by the Lovász number of a certain circulant subgraph (the 1-localization).
status_evidence.claim: The 1-localization Lovász-number question is referenced as motivation, not resolved.
